rubrics.criterion: After the solver patch, no definition of the retired fixed-column agenda pipeline remains anywhere in the gcalcli package: neither the fixed-width tab-separated and fixed-layout JSON renderer variants on the calendar interface nor the private row helper they shared, neither the retired row-assembly class (with its field evaluation and its two row-building methods) nor the fixed column layout class (with its header, row, and width methods) nor the module-level fixed-column evaluation function, and neither the stand-alone cell-escape and cell-padding helpers in the utils module nor the tab-separated row emitter on the printer. Under an equivalent sound refactor, none of these definitions (or trivial renames of them) survives in reachable production code.
rubrics.rationale: This is the core instance obligation: the selected prompt asks for complete removal of one specific retired pipeline that was spread deliberately across five production owners, so a patch that leaves any credited owner untouched is an incomplete job no matter how much other code it cleans.

rubrics.criterion: The solver patch does not preserve the retired pipeline in some indirect form: it neither moves the fixed-width rendering behind a flag, config option, or new CLI switch, nor re-implements the same fixed-layout row logic under new names (for example as a private rewrite of the layout, builder, escape/pad, or emitter helpers), nor comments it out instead of deleting it.
rubrics.rationale: The task's selected prompt explicitly rejects 'supporting' the old pipeline or re-adding output modes; retention by relocation or feature-gating would make the removal cosmetic while reopening the same maintenance ambiguity the task asks to close.

rubrics.criterion: Every location the solver removed was actually part of the retired pipeline: each deleted definition (or pruned binding) has no consumer among the supported program paths of the patched tree, and no definition that any live execution path needs was removed. Concretely, the patched package still renders the tab-separated overlay, the JSON overlay, and the human calendar display through their existing dispatch, and `import gcalcli` and every module import still succeed.
rubrics.rationale: Removal must be grounded in reachability for this instance, because the retired pipeline is deliberately twin-shaped with the live overlays; deleting definitions by name similarity instead of reachability is the central wrong path this case punishes.

rubrics.criterion: Every import statement that a removal edit touched was itself updated coherently: the patched tree contains no import binding of a name or module that the patch removed, and no import line retains a trailing comma, dangling parenthesized fragment, or other syntactic debris from pruning names.
rubrics.rationale: Two live modules were wired to the retired pipeline by extended import lines (binding the layout class, the retired row builder, and the escape helper); leaving those bindings behind either breaks the package import or re-imports nothing, so import-line repair is a required associated change of the core removal.

rubrics.criterion: No call site, constant reference, or name lookup left inside live code still targets a removed definition: grep-visible references (attribute access, function calls, registry entries) to the removed names and to the removed layout module are absent from the patched production tree.
rubrics.rationale: The injected cluster is mutually referencing (renderers call their row helper, the helper calls the builder, the builder and layout call the text helpers), so a partial removal leaves live-looking orphans behind; this rubric forces the associated edit chain to be closed rather than cut in the middle.

rubrics.criterion: The shared utility module keeps exactly the helpers that live code still uses: the retired cell-escape and cell-padding functions are gone while the agenda date/time formatting and all-day detection helpers they were placed beside — which the live output path calls — are unmodified.
rubrics.rationale: This instance locates two stranded helpers inside a high-traffic utility module next to visually indistinguishable live neighbours; the associated-change obligation is to prune the pair without thinning the live helper set a single item.

rubrics.criterion: The dedicated layout module of the retired pipeline is not left behind as a shell: either that file no longer exists in the patched tree, or (under an equivalent refactor) whatever file remains contains no fixed-column layout content — no field-order tuple, no width table, no padding or evaluation helpers of the old format.
rubrics.rationale: The case injected the retired format as its own module that live code still imports, which is why deleting only its contents but keeping the file would leave exactly the kind of 'old format module nobody listed' artifact the maintenance story is about.

rubrics.criterion: No module-level constant or table that served only the removed pipeline survives in the patched package: the fixed agenda field-order and per-column width tables (and any duplicate or hand-maintained copy of the fixed field order living in another module) are gone, with no orphaned constant left behind by the removal.
rubrics.rationale: The retired format's rigidity lived in data as much as code — two synchronized tables of field order and widths, one of them deliberately duplicated in a second module; cleaning the definitions without dissolving their data leaves an artifact that still pretends the format exists.

rubrics.criterion: The patched tree contains no leftover prose that presents the removed pipeline as an available or current feature: no comment, docstring, or module description anywhere in the package still describes fixed-width agenda rendering, pre-padded cell output, or the retired builder as if it had a role.
rubrics.rationale: The injected locations carry realistic docstrings explaining the retired compromise; leaving such text attached to surviving code misleads the next maintainer exactly the way the original leftovers did, so it is a case-specific cleanliness obligation rather than a generic style wish.

rubrics.criterion: The live machine-readable overlays survive the patch intact: the tab-separated row renderer and the JSON entry renderer that the normal query flow dispatches to for `--tsv` and `--json` still exist with their handler-driven column and key assembly unchanged, and their dispatch conditions are unmodified.
rubrics.rationale: The retired renderers were placed one method below their live counterparts and share their filters and idioms; the single most likely regression in this instance is confusing each pair, and the suite does not exercise either overlay path, so the patch alone must be inspected for this fact.

rubrics.criterion: The event-details machinery keeps its import-time behavior: the detail-handler registry is still built exactly as before, every handler class the registry instantiates is still defined and importable, and the module hosting them starts cleanly under `import gcalcli`.
rubrics.rationale: The retired row builder was injected into the details module right beside the registry, and the injected import-line extension sits in that same module; a clumsy removal that disturbs registry construction or module top-level execution would break every CLI path at startup.

rubrics.criterion: The full repository test suite passes on the patched tree with no test file modified, and no production behavior outside the removed pipeline changed: CLI flags, defaults, config handling, the calendar display, reminders, and the writable-field validation paths behave exactly as in the pinned revision.
rubrics.rationale: The validator compares the patched tree against the same executable suite used for the injected baseline; because the injected pipeline is unreachable by construction, every functional difference observed in the suite would be a regression introduced by the removal, not by the pre-existing state.

rubrics.criterion: The solver patch does not widen any user-visible surface in the course of the cleanup: no new CLI flag, parser argument, config key, environment variable, or output mode is introduced to route, feature-gate, or 'rescue' the retired pipeline, and no existing flag's meaning changes.
rubrics.rationale: Both task prompts explicitly require pure subtraction for this instance; an added switch would convert a dead-code cleanup into a behavior and interface change, which the case's compatibility boundary forbids.

rubrics.criterion: The patched package holds no newly created unused or dead definition as a side effect of the repair: nothing the solver added while refactoring (new helpers, wrappers, renamed copies, temporary compatibility shims) remains unreferenced by live code in the patched tree.
rubrics.rationale: A cleanup that deposits its own leftovers re-creates the exact problem the instance asks to eliminate, so the finished state must be held to the same liveness standard the removed pipeline failed.

rubrics.criterion: The solver patch confines its deletions to the retired pipeline: it removes no production definition that already existed at this revision outside that pipeline — in particular the long-standing unreferenced error-raising helper in the exceptions module, which predates this cleanup and sat outside its boundary, is still present and unmodified in the patched tree.
rubrics.rationale: Dead-code removal invites exactly one tempting overreach in this instance: a pre-existing, genuinely unreferenced production symbol exists in the tree and looks like the same kind of leftover the task targets, but the request scopes deletion to the retired cluster only, so unsolicited broadening is a case-specific failure even though it removes other real dead code.
